title: A check you have not seen fail is not a check.
Coverage is exposure; what survives a mutation is verification.
A test's name is a claim, and the body must prove all of it.
The oracle must not come from the code under test.
Every double is an unverified claim about production.
Determinism is a property of the test, not of the machine.
Design the suite from failure modes, not from the code's shape.
The cheapest test that can *observe* the defect wins — a runner that cannot observe it is not cheap, it is blind.
Every test declares its size, and the size's constraints are enforced.
absorbs: L2 U1 (decomposed; "FIRST" as a mnemonic is cut — see governance.md)

title: Every test names the defect it catches that no cheaper and no existing test catches.
The default gate's exclusions are derived, not hand-typed, and the count delta proves it.
What the gate cannot see is named in writing: coverage per risk area, production types with no test at all, and each gate's blind spot.
The runner must be able to observe the property asserted.
Wiring and registration have a smoke test: dropping a registration must fail something.
A double standing in for a real backend is bound by one contract suite executed against both, and a meta-test fails when a port has no such binding.
A double's behaviour is a claim about production: it honours every parameter the real thing honours, is concurrency-safe when the SUT fans out, and is never degenerate.
Stub at a boundary you own, at the lowest level that removes the cost, and never in the pure-domain layer.
A mock earns an assertion only when the call is itself the observable contract; never assert call sequences or counts as a proxy for an outcome.
Never assert on wall-clock time: no millisecond budget, no p95, no ratio of one duration to another. A real budget lives in a dedicated lane, excluded from the default run.
Never sleep to synchronise. Poll a condition with a timeout, gate on a latch the test controls, or sync on a signal the system itself emits.
absorbs: L2 U15 (a test's own timeout throws a distinguishable type, never the assertion's)

title: Non-determinism enters through an injected, pinned source: an injected clock for time, a seeded generator for randomness — and the instant and the seed are printed on failure.
Culture, timezone and locale are pinned wherever the test parses, formats, sorts or compares text, dates or money — and at least one case runs under a non-default one.
Tests pass in any order and alone. No shared mutable state without an unconditional reset.
Every shared external resource is namespaced per run or per worker and destroyed on teardown: port, path, database, container, volume, queue, task hub, orchestration instance.
No test reads ambient environment: no hardcoded absolute paths, no inherited env vars, no host network, no real credentials, no live third-party.
"Flaky" is a measured, quarantined, expiring state — never a retry budget.
Before calling a red run a regression, record the failing *fraction* and reproduce on the unmodified baseline.
Every test asserts something that can distinguish right from wrong.
The expected value is derived independently of the code under test.
Assert the tightest predicate the contract allows: no slack a plausible regression fits through, and an exact count wherever the count is the contract.
A negative or absence assertion is paired with a positive that proves the code ran.
Exception assertions name the exact type and the discriminating detail; every narrowed production catch filter gets a negative test.
Prove the arrange actually reaches the branch under test.
The asserted observable must have been produced by the act.
Red-proof every new or changed check against the exact expression it targets, and record the mutation and the observed failure.
Every claim about the suite is executed, not reasoned.
A filtered or scoped check asserts a non-zero subject count before it can pass.
A gate whose failure blocks nothing is documentation; say so or wire it in.
Name the one-line production edit that reddens this test; if the only edit you can name is an intentional decision, it is a change detector, not a test.
The test's name is a claim; the body proves every half of it.
Test observable behaviour through the surface a caller uses; no reflection into privates, and no test-only seam on a production type.
A failure-path test asserts the state of the thing that failed, not only the flag raised beside it.
Every reachable state has a test: empty, loading, partial, error, success, and the states reached only by failure or by a human not answering.
Every rule, filter, allowlist or predicate has at least one test driving the real production input-building path.
Assert at least one secondary observable: a neighbouring field, an emitted event, a counter, related state.
One act, visibly separated arrange/act/assert, no control flow in the body except idiomatic parametrization, and the varied input readable at the call site.
No degenerate fixture: the parameter under test is at a value where the mechanism can be observed at all.
A skipped test carries a reason, a tracking id and a re-enable condition; its code is unverified until it runs.
Query by role first; test id is the last resort.
Every interactive element under test is asserted to have an accessible name.
Accessibility is a failing test, not a review item, and every reachable state of a view is scanned — not just the happy one.
At least one axe (or equivalent) scan runs the full ruleset in a real browser.
Do not treat a green axe run as "accessible".
The keyboard path is tested separately from the mouse path.
Assert the association, not the presence, of a label or description.
Plant a real violation and watch the rule go red. An architecture rule you have not seen fail is presumed inert.
A rule over an empty matched-type set passes: assert the subject count is non-zero first.
Where the rule lives determines whether it can fire.
Prefer the coarser mechanism when it is airtight; keep the finer one only if it demonstrably fires.
The forbidden/allowed list is derived from what the repo actually contains, and drift fails the build.
Do not reach for an architecture rule to express a data-flow property inside a method body.

title: Writing or automating a scenario before the production code exists is what makes it BDD; writing scenarios after the code is done is test automation wearing Gherkin.
RETIRED 2026-08-22: evidence withdrawn — discovery-session attendance and role composition are not observable from a diff.

title: Write Gherkin declaratively — describe behaviour, not implementation.
Push interaction mechanics down into step definitions; keep the scenario text implementation-agnostic.
BDD/Gherkin pays off when scenarios stay tied to explicit business goals, not just feature-level examples.
RETIRED 2026-08-22: evidence withdrawn — team-composition-over-time is a team-process opinion with no diff-checkable falsifier.

title: A dormant (`@ignore`/skipped) scenario's step bindings are unverified code; un-ignoring is a required step of the change that lifts the block, not a follow-up.
Two components that deploy independently need a contract test; two that always ship together do not.
Consumer-driven by default; bi-directional spec comparison only when the provider is third-party or will not run verification.
The contract is verified against real provider code, never against a document or a mock of the provider.
Any in-process double standing in for a remote provider is bound by the same contract suite as the real client.
Where no contract test exists, a derivation check is the minimum: the client's route/DTO set is generated from, or diffed against, the server's.
A schema/contract test proves the contract rejects the wrong shape, not only that it accepts the right one.
Web-first, retrying assertions only.
No duration-based wait, and no network-quiet signal, as a readiness check.
Locate by user-visible role or label, not CSS or XPath.
Each spec is fully isolated: its own context, its own stubs, no ordering dependency.
Third-party and backend calls are stubbed at the route/transport level.
Trace on first retry; retries are bounded and are not a flake-hiding device.
E2E covers journeys, not fields.
Routing, unknown routes, and the error boundary each have an e2e test.
E2E sources carry a typed lint that fails on a missing `await`.
Integration means the real dependency engine, at the version production runs.
Schema and migrations are applied by the same mechanism production uses.
Assert the thing only the real backend can prove.
Wait on a readiness signal, never on a delay; wait before the first call, not after the first failure.
Each test or class gets its own namespace inside the shared dependency: its own database, schema, prefix, or container.
Record what the emulator does not model.
The integration lane is excluded from the PR gate only if what it covers is named, and it runs somewhere on a schedule.
One shared expensive fixture per class, disposed deterministically; never one container per test method.
Load tests validate a response-time goal under specified normal concurrent load; stress tests validate stability and graceful recovery under extreme load. Keep the two goals distinct.
Always load/stress test a Release build, never Debug or Development-mode configuration.
Define explicit pass/fail thresholds on the load test itself — not eyeballing a report — and only inside the performance lane (ruling C17).
Assert on percentiles and error rates, not averages.
Wire thresholds into the normal test-framework assertions so they gate CI like any other test — inside this lane only (ruling C17).
Know the tool's default abort behaviour: a threshold breach does not necessarily stop the run unless configured to.
Tier performance testing by pipeline stage: a fast smoke check gates PR/merge; heavier soak/load tests run nightly or per release, out-of-band.
Derive a baseline from multiple runs, not one, and gate on a percentage deviation from it rather than a single hard number.
Investigate every sudden performance regression rather than dismissing it as noise, and keep the perf suite from going stale.
Reach for a property test when a law exists; otherwise write examples.
A property must be shown to fail on a seeded bug, like any other check.
Bound the generator to the domain; an unbounded generator tests the framework's arithmetic instead of the code.
On failure, capture the shrunk counterexample and commit it as a normal example test.
Fix the seed and the case count in CI, and print both.
A snapshot is a change detector by construction; use it only where the whole shape is the contract.
Pair every snapshot with explicit assertions on the business facts that matter.
Scrub every non-deterministic field before comparing: ids, timestamps, ordering, machine names, paths.
Never bulk-accept. A snapshot diff is reviewed like a code diff, and the acceptance is part of the PR.
Keep snapshots small enough to read; a growing snapshot count is a quality metric in its own right.
Snapshot only stable, non-visual, serialised artifacts; never a component tree.
Specifically exercise midnight, month/day boundaries, DST transitions, and leap years with the fake clock.
Never mix a real clock and a fake one in the same test.
For precise business-logic/timer tests, advance fake time explicitly and deliberately, per test, rather than relying on auto-advance.
For UI/debounce-style dependence, prefer a clock that auto-advances realistically and flush on a condition — never a tick to an arbitrary fixed value.
Dispose timers created against a fake clock in teardown, the same as any other resource.
Positively assert that time-gated behaviour does not happen before its trigger, not only that it does happen after.
An advance issued immediately after starting an async host or loop is silently lost; sync on the subject's own emitted signal, never on a fixed delay.
Derive a poll or watchdog tick from its own timeout, so the check granularity scales with it; pin the derivation with a short-timeout test.
Pin a periodic/cyclic timer's cadence with split advances; one large advance cannot observe the tick size.
A shutdown/stop assertion follows the runner's actual chain of state transitions, not the assumption that the first stop call is terminal.
A unit test touches no network, filesystem, database, real clock, ambient env, or thread it did not create.
"Must mock everything" is a coupling finding about the production type, not a testing rule to work around.
Vary intersecting properties, not one axis at a time — bugs live at the combinations.
Phase coverage by dependency layer: leaves unmocked, mid-layer with leaves faked, top layer last.
Many assertions is fine; many indistinguishable assertions is not.
Lane speed is a lane-level report, never a per-test assertion.
Tighten a constraint deliberately (pool of 1, capacity of 1) to surface leaks and races in a test rather than in production.
The partition-key argument and a `WHERE c.userId`-shaped tenancy predicate are proven only against the real store, never a fake or an in-memory repository.
A `%Key%` app-setting binding expression resolves from host config only, never the worker's `appsettings.json`; an unresolved binding is silently disabled.
Serialize a class with `[CollectionDefinition(Name, DisableParallelization = true)]`; never the per-test `DisableParallelism`.
Pass `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken` into every awaited call that accepts one.
`IAsyncLifetime.InitializeAsync` returns `ValueTask` in xUnit v3; `DisposeAsync` overrides `WebApplicationFactory`.
`[Theory]` with `[InlineData]`/`[MemberData]` instead of duplicated `[Fact]`s; `MemberData` sources are deterministic and order-independent.
Categorise with `[Trait]`, and enforce the trait's spelling and placement with a reflection meta-guard.
One assertion library, house-wide; check the census, not the style guide.
Rebuild after editing tests before judging a failure; `--no-build` against a stale assembly reports phantom failures.
In a lane, run a scoped filter — never the full suite.
No `async void` tests, and no `async void` in code under test.
Never `.Result` / `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` / `.Wait()` in a test.
Every async assertion is awaited: `await Assert.ThrowsAsync<T>(...)`, `await Should.ThrowAsync<T>(...)`.
Do not sprinkle `ConfigureAwait(false)` in test bodies; audit it in the library under test instead.
Cancellation is behaviour: at least one test cancels mid-flight and asserts both the exception and the absence of a partial write.
`TimeProvider` is injected; tests use `FakeTimeProvider` from `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`.
An `Advance` immediately after `StartAsync` is lost; sync on the service's own emitted event, not on a delay.
Derive a watchdog's poll tick from its timeout (`tick = min(60s, timeout/4)`), and pin it with a short-timeout test.
Pin a `PeriodicTimer` cadence with split advances; one large advance cannot observe the tick size.
`StopApplication` does not stop a `WebApplication` host — assert the runner-shaped chain, not `ApplicationStopped` directly.
Do not use the EF Core InMemory provider. Use SQLite in-memory, Testcontainers, or the repository pattern.
Testcontainers images are pinned to a tag matching the production engine's major version; one container per fixture, not per test.
Every repository interface has a contract suite bound to both the fake and the real backend, and a meta-test fails when one is missing.
Query text, partition-key arguments and tenancy predicates are proven against the real store, and the lane that proves them is named.
Prefer `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` over a hand-built host; replace only boundary services.
Authentication and identity resolution must be exercised through the real pipeline by at least one test.
Outbound HTTP is faked at the `HttpMessageHandler`/WireMock boundary — never a real network call, never a mocked `HttpClient` type.
Assert the response contract: status code, `Location`/headers, problem-details shape — not only the body's happy field.
Drive an Aspire stack with `DistributedApplicationTestingBuilder` and wait via `ResourceNotificationService.WaitForResourceAsync` — never a sleep.
One AppHost at a time, and check for a second instance first when an emulator misbehaves.
Per-worktree data volumes are ephemeral, or explicitly cleaned; a wedged orchestration instance in a persistent volume poisons every later run.
Verify a Stryker survivor by hand before writing a test for it.
Scope Stryker by enumerated `--file`, not `--namespace`, and fail the harness when the mutant count is zero.
Mutation runs are scoped and on-demand, not a CI gate; the score is a measurement, not a threshold.
An ArchUnitNET rule must explicitly load every assembly containing the types it forbids, and be proven against a planted violation.
Prefer the reflection-based assembly-reference test where it expresses the same invariant; delete the ArchUnit sibling that has never fired.
Rank by CRAP, not by coverage percentage, when deciding what to test next.
Audit for untestable statics as a first-class finding: `DateTime.Now/UtcNow`, `File.*`, `Directory.*`, `Environment.*`, `new HttpClient()`, `Console.*`, `Process.*`, `Guid.NewGuid()`.
Parse and format with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` in production, and prove it with at least one test running under a comma-decimal culture.
Use `DateTimeOffset` at boundaries and assert the offset/kind, not only the instant.
Assert `[LoggerMessage]` `EventId`s via `FakeLogger`, never log message text.
Every hosted service / middleware / options binding gets a DI smoke test.
A guard clause's exception type is the contract; assert the type and the parameter name, not the message prose.
Verify snapshots: scrub GUIDs and timestamps, commit `.verified` files, review their diffs, and never accept in bulk.
NSubstitute (or the house mocking library) for one-off stubs; hand-written fakes in a shared testing project for ports with behaviour.
For load/stress testing, always use Release configuration, never Debug/Development.
Express NBomber load-test scenarios as plain async C# functions, assert thresholds via percentiles/error rates through the normal test framework, never averages.
Use `dotnet/crank` for ASP.NET Core/.NET runtime-level trend tracking and regression bisection across versions.
Reqnroll is the only live .NET BDD runner; never recommend SpecFlow.
`@ignore` is the only Gherkin tag that maps to a skip; every other tag becomes a `Category` trait.
Drive interaction with `user-event`, never `fireEvent`.
`findBy*` instead of `waitFor(() => getBy*(...))`.
A `waitFor` callback contains exactly one assertion and no side effects.
`queryBy*` only for absence.
`act()` appears only around timer advancement, never around render or user-event.
An act warning fails the test run.
Test the component, not the hook, unless the hook is itself a published unit.
A double-submit / double-click guard has its own test asserting the exact count.
Stub at the network boundary (MSW), never by mocking `fetch` or the API module.
Unhandled requests are an error, not a warning.
A default handler exists so the fallback is deliberate, and is itself schema-checked.
Assert the effect on the UI, and separately assert the request body — never only that the request fired.
Route/URL literals are generated, and the generator is verified in CI with a `--check` mode.
A fresh query client per test, retries off, and no shared cache across tests.
Never assert appearance, layout, or overflow under happy-dom/jsdom.
A class-name assertion is named as a contract test, not implied to be a visual one.
Media queries, `focus-visible`, `prefers-*` and scroll behaviour are browser-only.
The DOM-shim bootstrap is itself tested, or at minimum documented as load-bearing.
Per-file isolation is on, and shared globals are cleared after every test.
A skipped test carries the crash and the re-enable condition inline.
Time-dependent behaviour is driven by a fake clock, in the runner that owns one.
Fake timers are restored unconditionally, in a shared `afterEach`.
Animation is disabled in any test that asserts appearance or position.
Web-first assertions only.
No `waitForTimeout`, and no `networkidle` as a readiness signal.
Locate by user-visible role/label, not CSS or XPath.
Each spec is fully isolated: its own context, its own stubs, no ordering dependency.
Third-party and backend calls are stubbed at the route level.
Trace on first retry; retries are bounded and are not a flake-hiding device.
E2E covers journeys, not fields.
Routing, unknown routes and the error boundary each have an e2e test.
Assert typed lint on the e2e sources.
No DOM snapshot as a behavioural assertion.
Snapshot only stable, non-visual, serialised artifacts.
A pixel screenshot baseline is only worth it under a pinned rendering environment.
Prefer a computed, semantic visual assertion over a pixel diff.
A design-system rule that lives in `className` strings is guarded by a source scan that first proves it scans something.
The typechecker is part of the gate, and it is green before the suite is trusted.
Wire types are derived from a runtime schema, and parsing happens at the boundary.
A contract-parity test proves the schema rejects the wrong shape, not only that it accepts the right one.
Type-level expectations are asserted, not assumed.
`any` and non-null assertions do not appear in test code either.
Add or update a failing `tests/*.tftest.hcl` assertion before changing Terraform behaviour.
